records.title: Proposed architecture: common pen haptics API
records.summary: Apps ask for semantic effects; a shared core picks and times them; one adapter per vendor talks to the pen.
details: Layer 1, app: requests semantic effects (tool texture on or off, discrete events).
Layer 2, common pen haptics API (Rust in the research proposal): profiles, effect selection, timing, state, errors.
Layer 3, vendor adapters: OnePlus (Oplus SDK or Binder service), Xiaomi (Pencil Engine, once a haptic interface is verified), Lenovo (LPP, if documented), Huawei (NearLink, if documented).
Layer 4: the pen's own actuator.
Report unsupported capabilities explicitly. Don't imitate them with the tablet's vibrator.
Model the effect vocabulary on the HID Haptics page and the Windows waveform names, which are already vendor-neutral.

Built so far, host-side only: the route-side Rust workspace (repo-stylo2-interop-track) has a core with set profile, start and stop, and one adapter each for the OnePlus binder, direct BLE and the tablet vibrator. The BLE adapter is inert until a verified GATT profile is supplied. The OnePlus adapter reports unavailable until a real binder transport is attached.

It leaves intensity, duration, frequency and waveform capabilities off, because the reconstructed OnePlus interface has no such parameter (stylo2/docs/C-protocol.md, part 3). This follows the rule above about unsupported capabilities.
Its connection state has five values today. The route notes plan a seven-state lifecycle (adding Discovering, Initialising, Ready and Failed) once a real session flow is verified.
records.basis: Research inventory section 7, extended with the verified Windows model. Extended on 2 Nov 2026 from stylo2/docs/MISSION.md and C-protocol.md, with the state enum checked in the code.

records.title: Route B: independent BLE access and non-interference test (BLE inspector)
records.summary: Use the BLE inspector as an ordinary app to see whether it can find, connect to and write to the pen, and whether that disturbs OnePlus Notes or the system link.
details: Code: android/stylus-ble-inspector, with its README.md. Guide: stylo2/docs/G-local-continuation.md section 6. Playbook: PICKUP.md Step 5.

What it is: a non-root app that scans, connects, discovers GATT, reads, writes raw hex with or without response, subscribes to notify or indicate, and exports a plain-text evidence bundle. It flags likely pens with a name heuristic only, and hard-codes no UUIDs or manufacturer prefixes. minSdk 33, targetSdk 36 per its README.

Ask the owner first: installing it changes the tablet (CLAUDE.md). From the repository root: ./gradlew :stylus-ble-inspector:installDebug. Its README says it is compile-verified with passing JVM unit tests and not device-tested. Not rebuilt here.

It is not a sniffer. A second GATT client has its own connection and cannot see what Notes sends. The snoop (plan-hci-snoop-capture) answers what the bytes are. The inspector answers whether an independent app can connect and write, and whether that breaks Notes.
Step 1: grant nearby devices, start the scan, find the pen by the stylus candidate badge or by the address from dumpsys bluetooth_manager. Pair the pen normally first; the system manages that link.
Step 2: connect and discover. Record the whole GATT tree and export it. Redact Bluetooth addresses before recording anything here.
Step 3: look for a writable characteristic. Feed the export to stylo2_ble::recon::candidate_control_characteristics. A vendor, non-SIG UUID with a sibling notify channel ranks highest.

Step 4, non-interference: with the inspector connected, draw in Notes in split-screen. Do haptics still work? Does the system link drop (watch dumpsys bluetooth_manager)? If probing disrupts normal stylus input or Notes, stop and report before continuing.

Step 5, the moment of truth: write the exact bytes observed from Notes to the candidate characteristic, starting with the known-safe captured value. BLE writes change hardware state. Write only bytes captured from Notes; no blind fuzzing.
Order: steps 1 to 4 need no captured bytes. Step 5 needs the snoop result first.
Done means, for direct BLE: the inspector writes a captured value to a characteristic, the pen buzzes, and Notes still works with the inspector connected.

Rows in the E-prototype matrix this covers: 2 independent BLE discovery, 3 GATT services, 4 independent connection, 5 command access, and the non-interference rows 11 and 12 (plan-device-test-matrix).
Where to record: gap-second-gatt-client-access (steps 1 to 3), gap-second-gatt-client-disruption (step 4), gap-captured-write-buzzes-pen (step 5).
Results: none yet. Not run on a device.
records.basis: Transcribed from android/stylus-ble-inspector (README), stylo2/docs/G-local-continuation.md, PICKUP.md and CLAUDE.md on 2 Nov 2026. Not run on a device.

records.title: Physical-device test matrix (12 tests)
records.summary: Twelve tests for the Pad 3 and Stylo 2, each to be recorded with a method tag. None has been run.
details: Source: stylo2/docs/E-prototype.md. The result column is empty for all 12. Method tags: inspection, static, emulator, adb, physical. A row must not be passed from a successful build.
1. Detect the connected Stylo 2 (plan-ble-independent-access-test step 1; plan-pad3-readout bond check).
2. Independent BLE discovery works (plan-ble-independent-access-test).
3. Identify the available GATT services (plan-ble-independent-access-test).
4. Independent connection is possible (gap-second-gatt-client-access).
5. Haptic commands are accessible, and by which route (plan-route-a-poc-run, gap-captured-write-buzzes-pen).
6. Each vibration profile (the matrix says 0 to 3) gives which feel (gap-profile-integer-feel).
7. Start and stop behaviour.
8. Disconnect and reconnect handling.
9. App backgrounding and resume.
10. Behaviour after a tablet reboot.
11. Normal stylus input (MotionEvent) still works.
12. OnePlus Notes and system haptics are undisturbed.
Tests 11 and 12 are the non-interference guarantees. The doc makes them mandatory before any claim of success.

Expected behaviour by access situation, as the doc states it (expectations, not observations): ordinary install shows the service present and a PermissionDenied bind; service absent shows ServiceUnavailable; verified direct BLE or a vendor-authorised binder drives the pen; the fallback buzzes the tablet and says so.
Test 6 says profiles 0 to 3. G section 7 and C section 1.5 ask for setVibrationType 0 to 4. The PoC spinner offers 0 to 3.
Tests 7 to 10 have no gap record. They only make sense once a route works.
Results: none yet. Not run on a device.

records.title: Route B: HCI-snoop capture of OnePlus Notes (nine captures)
records.summary: Record the system's Bluetooth link while OnePlus Notes drives the pen, in nine controlled scenarios, to learn whether haptic control is GATT and what the bytes are.
details: Documents: stylo2/docs/J-capture-plan.md (method, schema, empty tables) and stylo2/docs/G-local-continuation.md sections 4 and 5. Playbook: PICKUP.md Step 5.

Ask the owner first. Turning on the HCI snoop log is a settings change, and Shizuku and BlueShark are extra apps (CLAUDE.md). Save snoop files in research/local/pad3/snoop/, which git ignores. Redact Bluetooth addresses in anything recorded here.

Principles: Notes is the oracle, so observe it and do not modify it. HCI snoop first, because it sits below the stack and sees the system's own link, which a second app's GATT client cannot. An external BLE sniffer only if the snoop misses packets, and an over-the-air capture of an encrypted link shows ciphertext unless pairing was captured. Absence of a packet does not prove absence of a path. Change one variable per capture and keep Notes' tool and canvas the same.

Option A, no root: BlueShark with Shizuku. Per the guide, BlueShark switches persist.bluetooth.btsnooplogmode to full, restarts Bluetooth, launches the vendor app, takes named markers while you draw, then decodes the snoop down to ATT with handle-to-UUID resolution. Shizuku is started over ADB and is not root.

Option B, no extra app: Developer options, Enable Bluetooth HCI snoop log, toggle Bluetooth, draw in Notes noting wall-clock times, adb bugreport, extract the btsnoop or btsnooz blob, open it in Wireshark and filter btatt.

Split-screen method: keep Notes and an observer (BlueShark markers or an adb logcat -v time terminal) side by side so Notes stays drawing-active. The guide expects both panes to stay resumed. First confirm haptics still fire in split-screen before trusting correlations. The inspector cannot sniff Notes.
First capture: one pencil stroke plus start and stop, just enough to see whether haptic control is ATT or GATT at all.
Capture 1, idle baseline: pen connected, Notes open, no drawing for about 15 seconds. Gives background and keepalive traffic to subtract.
Capture 2, Pencil profile: select Pencil in Notes. Look for the writes that differ from idle.
Capture 3, Eraser profile: select Eraser. Which bytes differ from capture 2.
Capture 4, Ballpoint profile: select Ballpoint. Which bytes differ from captures 2 and 3.
Capture 5, Pen profile: select Pen. Which bytes differ.
Capture 6, feedback on: draw so haptics fire. Note the activation write: handle and bytes.
Capture 7, feedback off: stop drawing, lift, or toggle off. Note the deactivation write.
Capture 8, disconnect and reconnect: detach and reattach the pen, or toggle its Bluetooth. Shows the teardown and re-initialisation sequence.

Capture 9, initial connection: from a powered-off pen, connect fresh with the snoop already running. Shows any handshake or session init before the first haptic (B4). This is the capture that shows whether a session or authentication step gates haptics.

Recording schema for every action: scenario, action, timestamp (and marker id), foreground app and binder caller if observable, binder calls if observable, bt_state (connected, for how long, role), packet direction, opcode (for example Write Request, Write Command, Handle Value Notification), ATT handle, characteristic UUID if resolvable from the capture's own discovery, payload hex, any error, and vibration_observed (yes or no). vibration_observed is the ground truth, so log it honestly.

Tables to fill: profile selection to write (handle, UUID, payload, bytes that differ from Pencil, vibration); feedback on and off (handle, UUID, opcode, payload, vibration); session and connection (direction, opcode, handle, payload, notes on handshake, CCCD subscribe, MTU or PHY).

Reading the result: ATT writes to one characteristic that line up with vibration make it the control attribute. Its UUIDs and encoder would fill stylo2_ble::Stylo2GattProfile, and the per-profile bytes check stylo2-oplus::wire::reported_code. A handshake in capture 9 is B4 session init and would be modelled as an Initialising state. No haptic-correlated ATT traffic at all means haptics are not a plain GATT write from the host: record that. It rules out direct BLE or points to another channel.
Attaching the pen marks when Bluetooth LE pairing should begin (c-pen-attach-handshake), so captures 8 and 9 should show it.

Where to record: gap-haptic-over-gatt (capture 6 and 7 against vibration), gap-haptic-command-bytes (captures 2 to 7), gap-session-handshake (capture 9), gap-oneplus-transport (when the service sends commands).
Results: none yet. Not run on a device.
records.basis: Transcribed from stylo2/docs/J-capture-plan.md, G-local-continuation.md, PICKUP.md and CLAUDE.md on 2 Nov 2026. Not run on a device.

records.title: Read-only Pad 3 read-out: identity, firmware, service, permission level, bond
records.summary: Read the tablet without changing it, with research/tools/pad3_readout.py or the equivalent adb reads, before any experiment.
details: Playbook: PICKUP.md Steps 1, 2 and 4. Raw commands: stylo2/docs/G-local-continuation.md section 3 and the appendix of PICKUP.md. Rules: CLAUDE.md.

Tool steps: check (model, project number, build, boot state, whether su works, which relevant apps are installed), identify, firmware (lists, hashes and pulls the pen-charger firmware, runs fwinfo.py), modules (root only), driver (module info and firmware-path strings), service, apk (pulls the installed pen service APK and records version, sizes and SHA-256; --packages for others), bluetooth, handshake (guided), poc-log, all.
Output goes to research/local/pad3/, which git ignores. summary.md there is redacted and safe to quote. raw/ is not.

The tool refuses any device command that is not on its read-only allowlist. The one exception is a temporary copy under /sdcard/Download/ to pull a file the shell user cannot read, deleted straight away.

service step: the pen service version; whether CoreService, the PENCIL_SDK action and safe.IOT appear; the protection level of safe.IOT read two ways (pm list permissions and dumpsys package of the declaring package); the permission allowlist XML files; which pen-client packages hold the permission.

Raw equivalents from G: adb shell dumpsys bluetooth_manager (bonded devices, redact the address); adb shell dumpsys package com.oplus.ipemanager | grep -i versionName; adb shell dumpsys activity services com.oplus.ipemanager; adb shell dumpsys package com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT; adb shell pm list permissions -d -g | grep -i -A2 'safe.IOT'; a grep for safe.IOT over /system/etc/permissions, /system_ext/etc/permissions, /vendor/etc/permissions and /product/etc/permissions.
If the protection level is signature, G says even a privileged install needs OnePlus's platform key, which closes the binder route to an independent app and leaves BLE or official authorisation.

Identify the tablet first. PICKUP.md says it is not established whether it is rooted or has a pen-fix module, and MISSION.md and stylo2/README.md describe it as stock and non-rooted. Root, if present, is for reads only.

G section 8 first-30-minutes order: adb and wireless debugging working so the tablet is free to hold; this read-out; install the inspector and confirm the pen is detectable (ask first); one HCI capture of a single pencil stroke with start and stop (ask first).

Answers: gap-iot-permission-level, gap-pen-firmware-directory, and, with the apk step and research/tools/aidl_check.py (PICKUP.md Step 2b, owner-approved), gap-aidl-matches-firmware. Also feeds if-oplus-ipemanager, dev-oneplus-pad3, if-cps8601-firmware and if-oplus-wireless-pen-driver.
Results: none yet. Not run on a device.
records.basis: Transcribed from PICKUP.md, CLAUDE.md, stylo2/docs/G-local-continuation.md and research/tools/pad3_readout.py on 2 Nov 2026. Not run on a device.

records.title: Research order
records.summary: The order from the research inventory, with progress noted. It focuses on OnePlus first rather than all four vendors equally.
details: 1. HiPaint's Stylo 2 integration: see which SDK it uses and how it starts. Not started.
2. The XDA implementation: covered, since it is this repository. The client and the privileged install are now documented separately.
3. The installed Oplus package: compare its services and permissions with the repository's interface. Not started.
4. OnePlus Notes Bluetooth traffic: learn whether haptic commands go per stroke or once per session. Not started.
5. Xiaomi Pencil Engine AAR: check whether it exposes real haptic output. Not started.
6. The common abstraction: start with OnePlus and add vendors only once their haptic interfaces are verified. Not started.

Route-side order for the Pad 3 session (PICKUP.md): host baseline, tablet check and read-out, Route A PoC, attach handshake, Route B (HCI snoop and BLE inspector, with the owner's go-ahead), then record. This refines items 3 and 4 above. Plans: plan-pad3-readout, plan-route-a-poc-run, plan-trust-boundary-isolation, plan-hci-snoop-capture, plan-ble-independent-access-test.

records.title: Reusability assessment
records.summary: Which components can be shared across vendors and which must stay vendor-specific.
details: Android stylus input: high reuse. Use the standard Android APIs.
Pressure and tilt processing: high reuse. Shared Rust or Kotlin implementation.
Haptic effect definitions: high reuse. Vendor-neutral effect model.
Xiaomi Pencil Engine: low reuse across vendors. Study its API structure.
Oplus Binder integration: OnePlus only. Dedicated adapter.
Xiaomi Bluetooth and HID implementation: Xiaomi only. Protocol-analysis reference.
Lenovo LPP and Huawei NearLink: unknown. Research separately.

records.title: Route A: run the unprivileged binder PoC
records.summary: Install the minimal PoC on the Pad 3 as an ordinary app, bind com.oplus.ipemanager, trigger a haptic, and read from the log which boundary refuses it.
details: Code: android/stylo2-poc, with its README.md mapping each outcome to a boundary. Playbook: PICKUP.md Step 3.
It is a plain Activity with four controls and a profile spinner: Bind and probe, Trigger (set profile and start), Stop feedback, Unbind. No root, no /system install, no firmware change.
Ask the owner first: installing the app changes the tablet (CLAUDE.md). Install it as an ordinary app only, never to /system and never with Magisk.
Build and install, from the repository root: ./gradlew :stylo2-poc:installDebug. The PoC README says it is compile-verified (assembleDebug) and not device-tested. Not rebuilt here.
Before it, run the service step of plan-pad3-readout. The protection level of safe.IOT is expected to predict the outcome.
Run: draw in Notes once to confirm the pen works; open the app; tap Bind and probe and read the log; pick a profile; tap Trigger and watch the pen; tap Stop feedback.
Capture: python3 research/tools/pad3_readout.py poc-log. It asks whether the pen vibrated. Every on-screen line is also sent to logcat under the tag Stylo2Poc (adb logcat -d -s Stylo2Poc).

Log stages: ENV (Android version, device, whether the IOT permission is granted, installed com.oplus.ipemanager version), DISCOVERY (queryIntentServices matches, each with exported and bind permission), BIND (bindService result or SecurityException, descriptor at connect), AUTHZ (getPencilConnectState as a harmless query), EXEC (setVibrationType, startFeedBackVibration, stopFeedBackVibration).

It attempts the bind even when the IOT permission is not granted. The repository's own client stops before binding in that case (if-oplus-call-sequence), so no earlier code shows what the platform does with an unprivileged bind.
Outcome: bind ok, AUTHZ accepted and the pen vibrates on Trigger means Route A works unprivileged and this app is the PoC.
Outcome: SecurityException or bindService false at BIND means B1, the permission is enforced. Go to Route B.
Outcome: bind ok but AUTHZ throws means B2, the service validates the caller. Capture Notes; consider official authorisation.
Outcome: bind and AUTHZ ok, calls return, no vibration means B4, the protocol or session gates the motor. Inspect it in an HCI snoop.
Outcome: version NOT INSTALLED or no discovery match means the service is not present or not queryable on this build.

Evidence to report: the firmware build and date, the pasted log, whether the pen physically vibrated, anything the log did not resolve, whether root or privilege was needed (no for this run), the device and build. Record works only if the pen vibrated.

If the descriptor line differs from com.oplus.ipemanager.sdk.ISdkAidlInterface, that is a finding: the interface differs on this build (gap-aidl-matches-firmware). Do not change the descriptor, codes or profile integers to make it work.
If BIND or AUTHZ is refused, that is the finding. Do not escalate privileges, grant the permission, spoof the package or signature, or use the upstream privileged app.

The PoC carries copies of the repository's Vibration enum and two AIDL files (identical when compared on 2 Nov 2026; it leaves out IpeFeature). Its profile spinner offers 0 to 3 only, not FUNCTION_VIBRATION (4).

Where to record: ENV line into gap-iot-permission-level; DISCOVERY and BIND into gap-service-discovery-and-bind; AUTHZ into gap-caller-validation-after-bind; EXEC into gap-unprivileged-execution; then, if the pen vibrated, gap-profile-integer-feel. Also add the row to the E-prototype matrix with a method tag.
Results: none yet. Not run on a device.

records.title: Route feasibility under stock, non-root, own-certificate limits
records.summary: Four routes to the pen's motor and how feasible each looks without root. None is verified to work.
details: Constraint for every row: stock OxygenOS, non-rooted, the app signed with its own certificate, no priv-app install, no firmware change.

Official OnePlus SDK (called Route C in the README): unknown. It would be the only legitimate path to privileged-equivalent access. No public SDK or docs were found by a desk search on 2 Nov 2026. It may need business terms and may not cover the Pad 3 and Stylo 2 (gap-oneplus-sdk-access).

Binder to com.oplus.ipemanager (Route A): B-feasibility concludes an ordinary app gets PermissionDenied, because the bind is gated by safe.IOT (at least privileged, reported) and possibly a vendor signature check. The only ways to hold the permission are a privileged install (root, out of scope) or vendor authorisation. That is the doc's conclusion. Whether the platform refuses an unprivileged bind has not been tested (gap-service-discovery-and-bind, gap-iot-permission-level).

Direct BLE (Route B): unknown, possibly impossible. It needs a verified writable haptic GATT characteristic, a command encoding, and proof that a second connection does not break the system link. Standard Bluetooth permissions can be granted, so that part is not the blocker.
Android vibrator fallback: available in principle. It plays the tablet's motor, not the pen, and has no profiles. A labelled degraded mode, not the goal.
Bottom line in B: no route to the pen's own motor is verified on a stock Pad 3.

Order of investigation in B: BLE reconnaissance first (cheap, no vendor dependency), official-SDK enquiry in parallel, fallback meanwhile. PICKUP.md orders the device work differently: read-outs, then Route A, then the handshake, then Route B. plan-research-order has a third order for the cross-vendor research.

Outcomes named in the earlier route brief (PICKUP.md before it became the unified playbook): direct BLE works, so fill Stylo2GattProfile, write a Kotlin GattTransport and set Availability.ble_protocol_verified; only the privileged binder path exists, so official authorisation is the only legitimate route; or in between, such as encrypted GATT or a second connection killing the system link.
stylo2_android::preferred_backend picks the authorised binder first, then verified direct BLE, then the tablet vibrator (code, checked 2 Nov 2026).

records.title: Four-step isolation of which boundary blocks third-party haptics
records.summary: Run discovery, binding, authorization and execution as four separate tests and read the blocking boundary off the first one that fails.
details: Source: stylo2/docs/H-trust-boundaries.md. Binder path only.
Premise: OnePlus Notes drives the motor today (owner-reported), so the motor, the link and the command path are presumed good, and B1 and B2 are the prime suspects (c-trust-boundaries).
Step 1, discovery: PackageManager queryIntentServices for com.oplus.ipemanager.ACTION.PENCIL_SDK. If it fails, the service is not exported or queryable to third parties (B2, export).
Step 2, binding: does bindService return true and onServiceConnected fire? A SecurityException or false points at B1 (the IOT permission) or a bind-time android:permission on the service.

Step 3, authorization: with the binder in hand, does a query such as getPencilConnectState succeed? If it throws or returns an auth error after a successful bind, it is B2 caller validation inside the service, not the Android permission.
Step 4, execution: does setProfile plus startFeedback buzz the pen? If it fails after authorization succeeds, it is B4 (protocol or session), not Android.

For each step record the exact exception, its message and the layer it came from (framework, Binder or downstream). A permission denial at step 2 says nothing about whether the protocol at B4 is authenticated.
The Route A PoC stages all four steps, so this plan is mostly a cross-check of its log (plan-route-a-poc-run).
The direct-BLE path (B3 and B4) is covered by plan-hci-snoop-capture and plan-ble-independent-access-test.
Mapping: steps 1 and 2 to gap-service-discovery-and-bind; step 3 to gap-caller-validation-after-bind; step 4 to gap-unprivileged-execution. The protection level (B1) is read by plan-pad3-readout.
